summary: Defines a MIB module for configuring Synthetic Sources for Performance Monitoring (SSPM) algorithms via SNMP. These sources generate artificial traffic for measuring network performance. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: To test how fast a road is, you can send test cars along it. This memo defines the controls for telling a device to send test traffic for measuring.

questions: what are synthetic sources for performance monitoring
how does an active probe mib work
subtitle: An SNMP MIB module for configuring test packet sources and sinks that measure network performance.

tldr.problem: The IETF had many performance monitoring tools but no standard way to remotely control an active probe that injects test traffic into the network.
tldr.mechanism: The SSPM-MIB defines general, source (profile and control tables) and sink objects, so a management application can configure a synthetic traffic source and the sink that receives it.
tldr.outcome: It fills the traffic generation gap alongside the APM-MIB and TPM-MIB, which cover monitoring and measurement. Because it can generate traffic, it carries denial-of-service and credential-exposure risks that the RFC covers.

today: RFC 4149 is a Proposed Standard (August 2005). The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Purpose and Terms
sections.content:
RFC 4149 defines a MIB module for Synthetic Sources for Performance Monitoring (SSPM). It is meant for the Remote Monitoring (RMON) framework, in cases where it is desirable to inject packets into the network so that their performance can be measured with the other MIBs in that framework. The RFC observes that existing IETF performance monitoring work does not explicitly define an active probe capability, and this module is built to fill that void.

A synthetic source is a device or embedded program that generates packets and injects them onto the path solely in support of performance monitoring. It may talk intrusively to existing application servers. Performance monitoring itself is made of traffic generators, measurement, data reduction and reporting.
sections.eli5: A synthetic source is a machine that sends pretend traffic just to see how the network copes with it, like a test drive.

sections.title: Design Goals
sections.content:
The module complements the performance management architecture being defined in the RMONMIB working group, and is defined within the context of the APM-MIB (RFC 3729). The stated goals are:

  • Extensibility: easy to extend to more protocols and applications.
  • Flexibility: supports both round-trip and one-way measurements.
  • Security: control of the source and sink is handled by a management application, and communication is recommended via SNMPv3.
sections.eli5: The controls should grow to cover new kinds of tests, work for out-and-back trips and one-way trips, and only let the right person press the buttons.

sections.title: Relationship to Other Work
sections.content:
Alongside the APM-MIB, the module is designed to be used with the Transport Performance Metrics MIB (RFC 4150), which define reporting. It uses the AppLocalIndex from the APM-MIB to map measurement configuration to the definition and reporting structures there.

The RFC surveys neighbouring work. IPPM defines metrics such as one-way delay and loss (the framework is RFC 2330). While this MIB was being developed, a one-way measurement protocol was found to be needed, which led to the IPPM work on the One-Way Measurement Protocol, whose control protocol is redundant with this MIB; the SSPM-MIB could be used as an alternative. DISMAN's pingMIB and tracerouteMIB (RFC 2925) probe connectivity, but the RFC says there is a fundamental difference between determining connectivity and determining its quality. RMON and RTFM are about passive measurement.

The overall picture is that traffic generation is covered by this module, monitoring and measurement by the APM-MIB and TPM-MIB, and data reduction was not yet addressed within the IETF.
sections.eli5: Other groups built tools that watch traffic or check whether a path exists. This memo adds the missing piece: a way to make the test traffic itself.

sections.title: Structure of the MIB Module
sections.content:
The module is rooted at sspmMIB, assigned as { rmon 28 }, with objects, notifications and conformance subtrees. The objects fall into three groups: general information, source configuration and sink configuration.

General information describes the probe: the resolution of its clock, the maximum skew of the clock over 86400 seconds, the clock source (using the NTP stratum idea, where 0 is unspecified, 1 is a primary reference and 2 to 255 is a secondary reference), and the minimum supported source frequency. A capabilities table lists the AppLocalIndex values for which SSPM configuration is supported.

The source is configured with two tables. The profile table defines reusable profiles, and the control table uses a profile to instantiate a specific measurement. The module takes an IP-centric view. The sink table configures the receiving end. For a round-trip test it lives on the same probe as the source, and for a one-way test it is on a different probe.
sections.eli5: There are three drawers of controls: one describing the machine's clock, one for how to send test traffic, and one for how to receive it.

sections.title: Source Profile and Control Settings
sections.content:
A profile row says what the test packets look like. Its type is an AppLocalIndex, and a row can only be created if there is a matching capabilities row. Settings include the packet size in bytes (counting data within the IP payload but not IP headers), how the packet is filled (random, pattern or url), the TOS value (default 0), the IPv6 flow label (0 to 1048575, default 0), a TTL (1 to 255), a Don't Fragment flag, loose source route addresses, and an IEEE 802.1Q tag where -1 means untagged. Username and password objects hold credentials for application-level tests.

A control row points at a profile and says how to run the test: the outgoing interface (zero lets the device decide), the destination address and type, whether the test is enabled, a timeout, the sampling distribution, and the frequency. With deterministic sampling, packets go out at a fixed spacing. With poisson, spacing is drawn from an exponential distribution based on the inverse of the frequency. First and last sequence numbers are also set here. If the destination is a DNS name, it is resolved before each measurement and not cached.

Setting a frequency lower than the device's reported minimum fails with an inconsistent value error.
sections.eli5: A profile is the recipe for one test packet. A control row says when and how often to send it and where to.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC states that the module may contain sensitive data such as user IDs and passwords, and that if security is compromised it could be a source of denial-of-service and other attacks. Objects that can be written are sensitive, and SET support in a non-secure environment without proper protection can have a negative effect on network operations.

The username and password objects can give unauthorized use of resources if read. Objects for packet size and rate can make denial-of-service attacks worse. The RFC suggests defining a maximum packet rate on the device and reporting it through the minimum-frequency object, which bounds what can be set for the control frequency. It also says the device should not allow source addresses other than those administratively configured on it. The sink table is described as having no security issues of its own.
sections.eli5: A machine that can send test traffic could be tricked into flooding someone, and the saved passwords must be kept secret. So only trusted managers should control it.

items.label: random
items.desc: Packet holds random data patterns, implementation dependent.

items.label: pattern
items.desc: The fill value is repeated until the packet reaches its size.

items.label: url
items.desc: A document from an http:, https: or ftp: URL is retrieved and used.
